children: Aluminum futures in the UK rose toward $3,290 per ton, underpinned by tight supply conditions.
The US-Iran war has disrupted aluminum supply from the region, with GCC production falling 44% year-on-year in July.
The region accounted for around 10% of global aluminum production before the conflict.
LME inventories remained close to a 36-year low, while SHFE stockpiles continued to fall, pointing to limited availability in the physical market.
However, the supply outlook could improve as several smelters restart and ramp up previously curtailed capacity, while others pursue expansion projects.

Increased Chinese exports could also help ease supply shortages from the Gulf, with aluminum exports from the world’s top producer climbing 17.2% year-on-year in August. Traders also appeared to shrug off a hawkish rate hike by the Federal Reserve, which sent the US dollar higher.
A strong US dollar typically weighs on dollar-denominated commodities by making them more expensive for global buyers.

title: Aluminum Advances
